description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its internal “representative workload performance suite” used in the benchmark lab to better reflect real customer traffic patterns. Today’s suite is considered too synthetic (limited sequence-length diversity, low concurrency realism, and weak coverage of streaming vs non-streaming request mixes), which has caused performance regressions to slip through when scheduler/batching/KV-cache changes look good on microbenches but regress on production-shaped traffic.

Project goal: add 10–15 new, customer-like traces into the benchmark-lab so that runtime/kernel/scheduling changes are evaluated against realistic distributions of (a) prompt + generation token lengths (including long-context prefill), (b) concurrency and arrival patterns (burstiness, mixed QPS), and (c) streaming behavior (SSE/streaming chunk cadence and tail latency). These traces will become gating inputs for CI perf checks (perf-canary) and will be documented and versioned so teams can reason about what the benchmark suite represents.

Scope:
- Define trace schema and acceptance criteria (privacy/anonymization rules, required metadata, replay determinism, hardware/model compatibility).
- Source traces from customer telemetry and/or synthetic reconstructions that preserve key distributions without exposing sensitive content.
- Build ingestion + validation pipeline in benchmark-lab (format conversion, normalization, replay harness integration).
- Add trace catalog and methodology documentation; decide how traces map to tiers (smoke, nightly, pre-release).
- Update CI/perf-canary gates and dashboards (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, TTFT, streaming chunk timings, error rates) and establish regression thresholds.

Non-goals:
- Changing the serving runtime itself (except small hooks needed for trace replay instrumentation).
- Building new customer-facing benchmark marketing materials (though PM may later reuse internal results).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Runtime Scheduling/Perf owners: Sofia Ivanova (EM), Marcus Reed (suite maintainer), Rina Kobayashi (bench harness).
- Runtime/Kernels advisors: Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato.
- SRE/Infra partners: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (capacity, canary gating, alerting), Allison Grant (observability signals).
- Product: Henry Cho (ensures alignment with customer-facing performance narratives).
- DevEx/Docs: Elliot Price, Wei Chen (documentation, internal/external doc alignment).

Timeline (typical 4–6 weeks):
1) Week 1: kickoff, requirements, privacy rules, trace schema + ADRs.
2) Weeks 2–3: trace collection/anonymization + initial 5 traces integrated; validation pipeline landed.
3) Weeks 4–5: expand to 10–15 traces; CI tiering + dashboards + regression thresholds.
4) Week 6: bake period; final go/no-go and rollout to default gating for runtime PRs.

Deliverables:
- Trace catalog (10–15 traces) with metadata and intended coverage.
- Benchmark methodology and acceptance criteria.
- CI integration (smoke + nightly + release gates) and dashboard updates.
- Decisions recorded (what counts as representative, how streaming is modeled, and how privacy is enforced).

files.description: Project overview page: motivation, goals, non-goals, stakeholders, timeline, deliverables, and how the new traces will be used in CI and release gates.

Spec for trace format/schema (required fields for sequence lengths, concurrency, streaming flags, timestamps), anonymization/redaction rules, and acceptance checks (determinism, replay fidelity, size limits).

Catalog of the 10–15 traces: short description, source (customer segment or synthetic), model family, prompt/gen token distributions, concurrency profile, streaming behavior, and which CI tier uses it.
ADR deciding how traces are split across smoke vs nightly vs pre-release suites; includes rationale on runtime developer velocity vs coverage.
ADR defining streaming metrics (TTFT, time-to-first-chunk, inter-chunk cadence, tail completion) and how the harness measures them consistently.
Policy page defining regression thresholds and exceptions for latency/throughput metrics on representative traces; includes error-budget-like treatment for perf regressions.
Dashboard documentation: what panels exist (p95/p99, throughput, TTFT, streaming cadence), how to interpret them, and alert routing/escalation.
Docs update plan for internal engineering docs: how to run representative suite locally, how to add a new trace, and how to interpret failures.
GitHub issue tracking ingestion pipeline work: parsers, normalizers, validators, and trace checksum/versioning.
Issue for implementing or refining streaming replay measurement (TTFT, chunk cadence) and ensuring harness supports mixed streaming/non-streaming.
Issue for integrating first batch of traces including metadata files, validation results, and expected baseline metrics.
Issue for integrating second batch of traces; includes long-context and high-concurrency cases.
Issue for optional final traces; includes edge cases like bursty arrivals and mixed sequence-length distributions.
PR adding trace schema validator, golden checks, and CI job that fails if traces are malformed or nondeterministic.
PR adding streaming metrics collection and reporting (TTFT, chunk timings) to benchmark-lab output artifacts.
PR landing initial trace files and metadata, plus baseline snapshot for expected performance ranges.
PR landing additional traces emphasizing concurrency and burstiness; updates catalog and CI tier mapping.
perf-canary issue to add representative smoke suite as a PR gate for runtime/benchmark-impacting changes, with clear failure output.
PR updating canary configuration to run smoke vs nightly suites and publish results to dashboards.
Kickoff discussion: why current suite is insufficient, proposed trace categories, owners, and timeline.
Thread debating how many traces should be streaming-heavy, what chunk cadence to model, and how to avoid gaming TTFT.
SRE + runtime thread: GPU capacity requirements for nightly runs, scheduling windows, and how to avoid noisy neighbors.
Platform/observability thread: which metrics to chart (p99, TTFT, streaming cadence), alert thresholds, and oncall routing.
DevEx coordination: where docs live, how engineers run the suite locally, and what guidance to include for interpreting regressions.
Linear epic tracking end-to-end workstreams: trace sourcing, ingestion pipeline, CI integration, dashboards, documentation.
Task for defining trace schema, writing validator, and adding unit/integration tests.
Task for streaming measurement definitions and ensuring replay harness produces stable results across runs.
Task for maintaining the trace catalog, assigning traces to smoke/nightly/release tiers, and documenting rationale.
Internal support ticket requesting reserved GPU capacity/time window for nightly representative suite runs; includes estimated runtime and cost.
Ticket to adjust CI runner disk/network limits to handle larger trace artifacts and benchmark outputs.
Spreadsheet summarizing each trace: seq length percentiles, concurrency, streaming share, expected baseline metrics, and CI tier.
Checklist/template ensuring traces contain no sensitive content, with sign-off fields and links to evidence (sampling, hashing, redaction steps).
Meeting transcript/notes: attendees (Runtime, SRE, PM, Docs), decisions on scope, and initial action items.
Go/no-go meeting transcript: readiness checklist (trace count, CI stability, dashboard signal quality) and rollout plan.
Email thread between PM and runtime leads aligning on what “representative” means, how results may be referenced later, and internal comms expectations.
Email review with observability owner on streaming metric definitions, instrumentation details, and dashboard naming/consistency.
Optional CRM notes capturing any customer coordination/permission follow-ups related to using anonymized telemetry-derived traces (high-level, non-sensitive).
